title: Normalized cubical maps before multiplication comparison
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the coherent profinite site, $r\geq0$, $J$ a normalized comparison between generalized-section and discrete $\mathbf Z^r$ actions, $C$ a cubical model with the cell coproducts, boundary, translation and contraction of [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-augmentation-evaluation], $K$ a finite subset-coordinate Koszul model [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution], and $B$ an equivariant unital $R$-algebra [lem-sfb-lattice-flat-twisted-chain-pairing]. Work in ordinary signed cochain tensors and derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $L=J(C.L)$, $X=tK(B)$ and $Z=B[0]$. There exist chain maps $\varepsilon,\Delta,E$ forming a normalized roof datum of [def-sfb-lattice-cubical-multiplication-data]. Explicitly, augmentation sends all vertices to one, the diagonal is the finite signed ordered-partition formula, evaluation on degree-zero tensor summands is the Kronecker coordinate formula $\delta_{A,I}c_pT^v$, and the left, right and double counit identities hold. This asserts neither compatibility with multiplication nor the denominator quasi-isomorphisms or derived roof equality.

proof.text: Reindex the integral chain degree $a$ as cochain degree $-a$. Its tensor sign $(-1)^a$ is unchanged because $(-1)^{-a}=(-1)^a$. Apply the integral diagonal theorem to the free generators of $L$: the chain-map, equivariance and counit identities are finite equalities with integer coefficients, so the identical sums of $R$-linear maps satisfy them internally. In particular $(\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta=\varepsilon$.  Construct augmentation and diagonal from their finite cell matrices; use the coproduct universal property to extend the integral chain-map, translation and counit identities.

For the normalized comparison J, use the signed evaluation of the augmentation-evaluation theorem on the degree-zero algebra complex. Its coordinate calculation gives c_p T^v on matching coordinates and zero off the diagonal. If C differs from its chosen cubical model, transport along the unique cell-preserving isomorphism; the prescribed coproducts, boundary and translation determine that isomorphism. The three normalization formulas fix the data, while the integral counits give the three remaining equations.
